notes: Batch 6 of article-10-landmarks: LM301–LM336, designated 2022–2026 — the last 36 landmarks in DataSF 97yj-54sx. Every PDF carries a text layer (pdftotext -layout; txt6/). Read by nine parallel readers writing one notes file per report, each raw.text checked mechanically against the text layer before assembly. LM301–LM321 and LM336 are the ordinance with the Planning fact sheet or full designation report (LM316's PDF is the 2016 report alone, with no ordinance); LM322–LM335 are the Board's April 2026 omnibus — each PDF the Clerk's cover memo, the ordinance and a short fact sheet, some with older DPR 523 or context-statement pages attached.

coverage.remaining: None in LM301–LM336, and none left in the source: LM336 is the highest number DataSF lists. Not cited: PDF pp. 11–21 of LM324 (an image-only printout of a 2021 SF Heritage post on the American Indian Historical Society; OCR would add the 1967 Planning approval, the 1969 Alcatraz committee meetings, Wassaja from 1973 and the Costos' deaths). The full designation reports behind the fourteen 2026 ordinances (LM322–LM335) are not in these PDFs.
coverage.note: 36 reports read: 667 findings, 608 resolved, 562 published on 99 pages (29 seeded), 46 declined — nearly all repeats of what a page already carried from the LGBTQ, Mission Dolores or professionals-biographies statements or an earlier landmark report — 55 unresolved (the Westwood Park gateway pillars and Harvey Milk Plaza's rainbow flag stand on no parcel; 24th Street, Castro and Polk Street numbers with no EAS record; four Marina condominium or split lots) and 4 rejected (demolished buildings). Report-day owners, the living man the House of Latin Rock is known for and the Gregangelo Museum's living creator-owner are left out; notable past occupants taken (Herbert Rosener, Mel Novikoff, Howard and Sue Bailey Thurman, Henri and Tomoye Takahashi, Bob Ross, Warren C. Perry, Michael Rios, George W. Green and others).
